where: Section 3 pin list (and repeated in Quiz Q7)
problem: The pin-number-to-signal order is reversed. Pin 12 is AD0 and pin 19 is AD7; pin 21 is A8 and pin 28 is A15. Writing 'Pins 12-19: AD7-AD0' and 'Pins 21-28: A15-A8' reads as if pin 12 = AD7 and pin 21 = A15, which would make a student wire the bus backwards.
fix: Pins 12-19 are AD0-AD7 (pin 12 = AD0, pin 19 = AD7). Pins 21-28 are A8-A15 (pin 21 = A8, pin 28 = A15). Q7 answer: 'Pins 12-19, AD0-AD7, carry the low address byte during T1.'

problem: The diagram shows a separate 'Data buffer' with note 'D7-D0', but the 8085 has no separate D7-D0 pins: the low address and data share AD7-AD0. The figure contradicts Section 1 ('address/data buffer carries the low address byte AD7-AD0, then data') and can make a student think there is a dedicated data bus.
fix: Label that node 'Address/Data buffer' with note 'AD7-AD0 (address in T1, then data)' and keep the single buffer facing the pins.

problem: AC is defined only as the carry from bit 3 to bit 4. In subtraction the same flag is set by a borrow. Students who only see the addition wording get confused by SUB and by DAA after subtraction.
fix: Add: 'In addition AC = carry out of bit 3. In subtraction AC = borrow into bit 3 (borrow from bit 4). DAA uses AC and CY together to correct BCD results.'
